analysis:
At the Jewar foundation-stone ceremony on 27 June 2026, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the state aimed to raise renewable energy generation capacity to 20,000 MW within two to three years, from about 6,000 MW at the time.

MNRE state-wise data showed Uttar Pradesh's installed renewable capacity (excluding large hydro) at about 6,182 MW as of 28 February 2025, consistent with the CM's stated starting figure. The state's Solar Energy Policy 2022 carried a separate target of 22 GW of solar by 2026-27.

The 20,000 MW target has a window of roughly 2028-29, so it remains open and is recorded as in progress.
notes: The 20,000 MW statement was made in June 2026 with a 'two to three years' horizon; the deadline field uses the outer three-year mark (30 June 2029). Quotation is PTI-sourced reporting, not a transcript, so not marked verbatim. State-wise RE figures are as reported by MNRE; a current UP-specific figure as on the claim date was not independently fetched.
